title: Doubao App Launches Store Discovery: Merchants Can Batch Mark Locations on Maps, with Group-Buy Ordering and One-Click Navigation Closing the Loop in Chat

content_html:
According to Dujia, ByteDance's Doubao app recently launched a "Find Stores" feature that plots matching merchants in batches on a map. Users can tap a store icon to go directly to the merchant page to view group-buy packages and place orders, or start navigation with one tap, consolidating store discovery, price comparison, ordering, and travel into a single chat page. This is another implementation for Doubao in local life scenarios, following the launch of the "Use Doubao for Travel" super entry point and the integration of ride-hailing, navigation, and hotel booking capabilities.

Unlike previous AI restaurant recommendations that returned only text lists, this feature visually presents store locations through a map layer. Listings include per-person spending, business status, ratings, group-buy packages, and vouchers. Users can also add conditions such as party size, main meals or late-night snacks, and budget to let the AI filter again, saving them from repeatedly switching among chat, maps, and group-buying apps. Search is not limited to food: users can enter keywords in the search bar to find nearby places such as attractions, hotels, gas stations, and leisure and entertainment venues, essentially embedding local life search into AI chat. For merchants, the map scenario also adds an exposure channel for Douyin ecosystem merchants.

At the industry level, Meituan and Xiaohongshu had previously launched standalone map-based store-finding entry points. Their approach is also to overlay stores on a geographic location layer, shortening the conversion path from "viewing a location" to ordering group-buy deals and buying vouchers, and building capabilities around a closed loop for in-store transactions.

Doubao emphasized that this move is not about competing for the group-buying business. Its core remains being a good AI assistant and solving the pain point of natural-language Q&A being disconnected from offline actions. As the value of general Q&A becomes increasingly limited, connecting recommendation results to in-store consumption and travel navigation is becoming a common direction for AI assistants to extend into offline life services.
